claim: Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer core rank equality for every elliptic curve over Q
scope_notice: A comprehensive finite research taxonomy, NOT an enumeration of every imaginable mathematical idea.
official_core_vs_refined: Core all-curves rank equality is distinct from the stronger optional refined leading-term route.

routes.name: Analytic L-function / complex derivatives
routes.scope: All E/Q only if arbitrary vanishing order can be controlled
routes.lever: Relate the order and leading derivative of the complete L(E,s) at s=1 to canonical global arithmetic quantities.
routes.bridge: Prove unconditional upper and lower comparisons with Mordell–Weil rank, uniformly in analytic rank >=2.
routes.failure: Finite Euler coefficients, numerically small L-values, or parity cannot certify order of vanishing.
routes.exper: For a declared rank-2 curve, identify a provable exact derivative/height identity and list missing assumptions.

routes.name: Descent and Selmer bounds
routes.lever: Use n-Selmer and descent to bound algebraic rank and determine torsion.
routes.bridge: Control Sha obstructions and connect algebraic rank bounds to complex analytic order for every E/Q.
routes.failure: An upper bound on rank does not determine analytic order; finite descents may leave unresolved Sha.
routes.exper: Reproduce a complete 2-descent for E1/E5 and compare proved rank bounds to certified analytic data.

routes.name: Gross–Zagier / Kolyvagin (low rank)
routes.lever: Heegner heights and Euler systems yield rank equality and Sha finiteness in these cases.
routes.bridge: A genuinely new mechanism for arbitrary higher vanishing orders; the known theorem cannot simply be re-used as all-rank proof.
routes.failure: An argument that only produces one independent rational point cannot certify arbitrary rank.
routes.exper: Formalize a known rank-one instance, documenting each cited theorem and hypothesis.

routes.name: Higher-rank Euler/Kolyvagin systems
routes.lever: Find rank-sensitive compatible cohomology classes and sufficiently strong Selmer control.
routes.bridge: Existence, nontriviality, higher-rank bounds and noncircular link to higher complex derivatives for every E/Q.
routes.failure: Classes may vanish or bound only special primes and curves; 'higher-rank' labels do not confer needed rank inequalities.
routes.exper: State a candidate higher-rank norm-compatibility and reciprocity law with a falsifiable concrete example.

routes.name: Higher Gross–Zagier/height formulas
routes.lever: Generalize derivative-to-height identities beyond first derivatives, with independent cycles/points.
routes.bridge: A nondegenerate global height determinant matching the order for arbitrary E/Q.
routes.failure: Derivative formulas under special sign or CM hypotheses do not automatically cover all curves.
routes.exper: Locate a rank-2 specialization with a theorem-level equality and verify its hypotheses without assuming BSD.

routes.name: Iwasawa main conjectures
routes.scope: p-adic and residual representation restrictions, selected ranks
routes.lever: Compare p-adic L-functions with Selmer modules; current literature gives new cases and selected p-parts of BSD.
routes.bridge: Remove all local/residual/rank restrictions and bridge p-adic comparisons to every complex analytic vanishing order.
routes.failure: A p-part of a formula, or result at one ordinary prime, is not the full complex or integral BSD formula.
routes.exper: Audit exact local hypotheses of a published main-conjecture theorem; list excluded cases E,p.

routes.name: p-adic heights and regulators
routes.lever: Relate p-adic derivatives, heights, Selmer ranks and regulators.
routes.bridge: Unconditional nondegeneracy, exceptional-zero accounting and archimedean comparison in all ranks.
routes.failure: A zero of a p-adic L-function can arise from local exceptional factors and need not measure complex analytic rank.
routes.exper: Compare ordinary vs supersingular and exceptional-zero hypotheses for one curve and one p.

routes.name: Bloch–Kato / motivic / ETNC routes
routes.lever: Connect motivic cohomology, special values and Selmer arithmetic in a general conjectural framework.
routes.bridge: Prove applicable noncircular comparison theorems without assuming conjectures equivalent to the desired BSD conclusion.
routes.failure: Replacing BSD with Bloch–Kato or ETNC as a premise is a conditional reformulation, not a proof.
routes.exper: Draft precise implication with all source theorems separated from open conjectures.

routes.name: Finiteness of Tate–Shafarevich groups
routes.scope: All E/Q required for general refined route
routes.lever: Prove Sha(E) finite through duality, descent or new uniform arithmetic estimates.
routes.bridge: Uniform finiteness at every relevant prime for arbitrary E; still need separate complex analytic rank link.
routes.failure: Sha finiteness by itself does not prove analytic rank equals algebraic rank.
routes.exper: Produce an explicit family of Selmer classes and isolate the exact missing finiteness bound.

routes.name: Automorphic / trace formula / spectral routes
routes.scope: Modular automorphic L-functions attached to E/Q
routes.lever: Find spectral or trace identities translating central vanishing into arithmetic rank.
routes.bridge: A spectral identity strong enough to determine exact multiplicity for every E and connect it to rational points.
routes.failure: Modularity provides continuation and a functional equation but not rank equality.
routes.exper: Write a proposed trace identity as a theorem with domains, multiplicities, and a counterexample search.

routes.name: Twists, congruences and specialization
routes.lever: Transfer knowledge between related elliptic curves using twists, Hecke congruences and specialization.
routes.bridge: A rigorous all-curves coverage theorem with control of rank and leading terms through exceptional fibers.
routes.failure: A theorem for a dense or positive-proportion family is not a theorem for every E/Q.
routes.exper: Prove exact coverage for a finite candidate family and list omitted curves; test degeneration at excluded primes.

routes.name: Arithmetic statistics and average rank
routes.lever: Prove average Selmer/rank statements and large families of known cases.
routes.bridge: Replace density or average claims with an all-curves theorem, or a universal reduction covering every excluded case.
routes.failure: Probability 1 or density 1 does not imply a property of every curve.
routes.exper: Record the exact height ordering and exceptional-set quantifiers of an existing rank result.

routes.name: Direct computation and certified examples
routes.lever: Use exact point search, descents, modular symbols and certified analytic interval arithmetic.
routes.bridge: A uniform proof covering unbounded conductors and arbitrary ranks, not merely a growing table of examples.
routes.failure: Numerical L-derivative zero tests and finite prime counts cannot prove an all-curves theorem.
routes.exper: Replicate E1/E5 local counts, then extend to a high-rank example with certified algebraic/analytic evidence.

routes.name: Partial Euler-factor agreement (MathOS 007)
routes.scope: Infinitely many primes in proper congruence classes
routes.lever: Identify precisely what selected local arithmetic information does not determine.
routes.bridge: A new theorem using sufficient complete global information, not merely a partial Euler product.
routes.failure: E1 and E5 have differing known ranks but matching counts for every p≡3 mod4; the argument cannot imply BSD.
routes.exper: Use the MathOS 007 classical counterexample as an adversarial negative control for every local-data proposal.

routes.name: Formal theorem verification
routes.lever: Lean or other proof assistants can verify well-stated algebraic, analytic and arithmetic lemmas.
routes.bridge: A mathematically complete general theorem must first be identified, encoded, proved without hidden assumptions and linked to the official target.
routes.failure: Passing finite tests or formalizing a conditional identity does not prove missing hypotheses.
routes.exper: Extend Lean beyond conditional character cancellation to an actual finite-field point-count theorem with explicit finite-field axioms.

routes.name: Logical counterexample (disproof branch)
routes.lever: Establish a single rigorously verified inequality between analytic and algebraic ranks.
routes.bridge: Unconditional proof of both exact ranks/orders for the same E with no numerical or conjectural gap.
routes.failure: Large computed discrepancy, inconclusive descent, or assumed Sha finiteness is not a counterexample.
routes.exper: Write a complete certificate format for analytic order and Mordell–Weil rank before choosing cases.

routes.name: Direct universal rank bridge
routes.lever: Prove both r_alg≤r_an and r_an≤r_alg unconditionally by separate, noncircular arguments.
routes.bridge: Both inequalities for all E, including analytic rank >=2 and all bad reduction types.
routes.failure: Stating either inequality as a conjectural lemma without proof is circular.
routes.exper: Inventory every inequality from published results and identify exact high-rank missing hypotheses.

routes.name: Universal refined leading-term formula
routes.scope: All curves with the precise refined BSD normalizations
routes.lever: Relate the first nonzero complex L-derivative to periods, regulators, torsion, Tamagawa numbers and Sha.
routes.bridge: Prove Sha finiteness and every factor/normalization for all curves, plus analytic/algebraic rank equality.
routes.failure: A p-part, special-curve computation or formula assuming finiteness cannot establish the unrestricted refined claim.
routes.exper: Audit all factors for E1 and E5 and identify which are sourced rather than proved.
